summary: This lecture is already-public support for Borderland's easy-money corruption anchor and creates held routing pressure for the British world game as a finance, law, schooling, local-elite, and force machine before America adds the dollar.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: A society can become wealthy by protecting dirty or stolen money, but that easy-money model drains morality, energy, openness, cohesion, and soul.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Borderland page already uses this source for the durable corruption-drains-motion anchor, and the episode read already links the matching corruption-drains-motion marks. This intake keeps any further provenance work concept-scoped instead of reopening completed Borderland linkage.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: keep this lecture as the negative borderland test where wealth without morality drains the energy, openness, and cohesion that make a society historically alive.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Borderland owns the energy/openness/cohesion diagnostic and the moral corrosion of easy money. It should not absorb the whole British Empire, Bank of England, offshore finance, Rhodes, or dollar-hegemony prehistory.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use as bounded Power pressure only when comparing how Parliament, contract law, property doctrine, the Bank of England, and offshore financial centers convert capital protection into an operating reality people trust and organize around.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Power owns symbol-to-reality conversion. Debt owns the obligation form, Dollar Hegemony owns the later American reserve operating system, and Borderland owns the moral-energy diagnostic.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold for a future debt chronology pass: the Bank of England changes lending from a king's personal risk into a national obligation that survives the ruler and binds the people as debtor body.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Debt owns national obligation and public repayment machinery. This source is an early-modern origin layer, not a standalone Bank of England page.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use only as prehistory for the later American dollar game: Britain creates a legal-financial world game through capital protection, offshore finance, colonial extraction, schooling, and naval force; the next class adds U.S. dollars and makes the game easier and more universal.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Dollar Hegemony starts where the dollar becomes the value standard and demand machine. The British source supplies ancestry, not the main dollar operating system already carried by America's Game.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold the English-schooling layer as education pressure only when comparing schools as imperial desire machines: English education teaches colonized elites to want British mobility, Oxford/Cambridge access, and Rhodes-style selection.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Education owns formation of desire and elite mobility. Secret Society owns the hidden-network claim; Power and Strategy own the finance and force surfaces.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold Rhodes-style imperial bonding and intermarriage/religion/secret-society capital trust as caveated coordination pressure; do not treat the lecture as a membership ledger.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Secret Society receives the trust and selection machinery only where Jiang names it as coordination technology. The broader world game remains finance, schooling, law, and force.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use the doping-game ending as a game-theory comparison only if future compression needs a short-term immoral advantage mechanism: one player cheats, wins, and forces everyone else to adopt the poisonous tactic or be eliminated.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Game Theory owns the short-term payoff trap. Borderland owns the long-term moral and civilizational corrosion.

new_lens_seeds.title: British World Game As Finance-School-Force Machine
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Empire becomes a playable world game when capital protection, national debt, contract law, offshore laundering, local-elite exit incentives, English schooling, elite bonding, and naval force make people and colonies cooperate with their own extraction.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism connects this lecture to America's Game, Dollar Hegemony, Power, Debt, Education, Secret Society, Strategy, and Borderland without reducing any one page to a British Empire topic.
new_lens_seeds.reason: Hold as a routing seed. Borderland already carries the public moral-corruption mechanism, and Dollar Hegemony / America's Game already carries the later American world-game surface. A British-world-game page would duplicate several existing lenses unless a future cluster proves a narrower reader need.

chronology_notes.note: Dated 2026-01-22, this lecture is the British predecessor to the January 27 America's Game source: Britain builds the game through capital protection, offshore finance, local elites, schooling, and naval force; the next class adds U.S. dollars and universalizes the game.

Jiang's sequence runs from the Thirty Years' War to the 1688 Glorious Revolution to the 1694 Bank of England: capital seeks security, Parliament becomes the real sovereign, and lending to the nation replaces lending to a mortal king.

The lecture adds a negative version of the borderland scorecard: silver wealth makes Spain lazy, insular, arrogant, and overextended, while later offshore wealth corrupts the first-world hosts that absorb stolen money.

next_actions.action: No immediate public prose mutation is needed: Borderland already carries `lens-point:borderland-corruption-drains-motion`. If episode-to-lens provenance becomes necessary, add it as a separate concept-scoped link batch rather than inside this compact intake.

Do not create standalone The World's Bank, Bank of England, British Empire, Offshore Financial Center, Money Laundering Empire, Glorious Revolution, Parliament Protects Capital, Rhodes Scholar, English Education Empire, East India Company, Opium Trade, Local Elites Steal Their Country, Spain Silver Poison, or Olympic Doping Game pages from this source alone.

If synthesis follows, compare this source with the Dutch Golden Age, America's Game, Capital of Evil, and Dollar Hegemony records before deciding whether the held British-world-game seed needs a workflow review or a public router paragraph.

If provenance maintenance follows, keep it concept-scoped: Borderland links are already present; only add Bank of England, debt, education, secret-society, or game-theory read links if a future page has exact stable anchors that match those narrower mechanisms.
